 Coram : S.G. Mehare, J.
 Dated : January 20, 2023
 Per Court:-
 1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned APP for  the State and learned counsel appointed for the respondent  no.2/victim.
2. The fact appears that the applicant and victim had love  affair.
On the day of the alleged incident, the victim was 16 years old.
She eloped with the applicant and went to Pune.
Her parents lodged  the missing report.
The police apprehended them and brought to the  police station.
Her family members and police from Mukhed were  also there.
However, Pune police set them free.

Her first statement  was recorded on 15.08.2022 and her statement under Section 164 of Hanumant Shivaji Gutte vs The State Of Maharashtra And Another on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61440671/

sentences.text: It appears  that she was in the custody of her parents.

 tutoring her cannot be ruled out.
There is no evidence that when she  eloped, she resisted or attempted to flee away.
They were in  relationship for two years.
However in those two years, there were  no complaints.
These circumstances have bearing on the case.
What  are the discrepancies as pointed out by the respective counsels, is  undoubtedly the matter of evidence before the trial Court.
Though it  has been pointed out that the Sessions Court rejected the bail and  observed that the trial is likely to open, the trial is yet not  commenced.
The victim was in advanced age.
She was knowing the  consequences of act she was doing.
She never resisted the applicant  during her stay with him at Pune.
3. Bearing the above facts in mind, the Court is of the view  that the application deserves to be allowed.

Hence, the following  order :
 ORDER  (i) Bail Application is allowed.

(ii) The applicant, Hanumant Shivaji Gutte, be released on bail on executing P.B. and S.B. of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees fifty thousand) with one solvent surety in the like amount in connection with Crime No.249 of 2022, registered at Mukhed Police Station, District Nanded for the offence punishable under Section 363, 366-A, 376, 376(2)(N) (J) of the Indian Penal Code and Section 4 and 6 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012 on the Hanumant Shivaji Gutte vs The State Of Maharashtra And Another on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61440671/
2 conditions that;
922-ba-2081-2022.odt (a) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution witnesses.
(b) The applicant shall not contact the victim in any mode or manner, till conclusion of the trial.
(S.G. MEHARE, J.) Mujaheed//
